record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^N be a bounded convex domain, and let {γ_k} be a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments, meaning that γ_k([0,1]) eventually avoids every compact subset of Ω while the endpoints satisfy γ_k(0) → p and γ_k(1) → q for two distinct boundary points p,q ∈ ∂Ω. Define the boundary cluster set Γ({γ_k}) = {x ∈ ∂Ω : there exist indices k_n and parameters t_{k_n} ∈ [0,1] such that γ_{k_n}(t_{k_n}) → x}. If p and q are two distinct points of Γ({γ_k}), must one of the following two alternatives always hold: either the open real segment {tp + (1−t)q : 0 < t < 1} lies in Ω, or the closed real segment {tp + (1−t)q : 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} lies in ∂Ω and the complex affine line through p and q, namely (ℂ(p−q)+q), does not meet Ω?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.5. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Let {γk} be a sequence of non-visible geodesic segments and let Γ({γk}) := {p ∈ ∂Ω : ∃{tkn } ⊂ [0, 1] : limn→∞ γkn(tkn) = p}. If p, q ∈ Γ({γk}) and p ̸= q then • either {tp + (1 − t)q, 0 < t < 1} ⊂ Ω, • or, {tp + (1 − t)q, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1} ⊂ ∂Ω and (C(p − q) + q) ∩ Ω = ∅.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain, equipped with its standard structure as an open convex subset of $\mathbb{C}^N$. A geodesic segment in $\Omega$ is a continuous map $\gamma:[0,1]\to\Omega$ (for instance, a real geodesic for the Kobayashi distance, or any reasonable curve; the statement below is intended for arbitrary geodesic segments). Consider a sequence $\{\gamma_k\}$ of such geodesic segments $\gamma_k:[0,1]\to\Omega$ that is non-visible in the following sense: for every compact subset $K\subset\Omega$ there exists $k_0$ such that, for all $k\ge k_0$, the image $\gamma_k([0,1])$ is disjoint from $K$, while the endpoints converge, $\gamma_k(0)\to p$ and $\gamma_k(1)\to q$, to two distinct points $p,q\in\partial\Omega$.

Define the boundary cluster set
$$\Gamma(\{\gamma_k\}) := \{x\in\partial\Omega : \exists\, k_n\to\infty,\ \exists\, t_{k_n}\in[0,1]\ \text{with}\ \gamma_{k_n}(t_{k_n})\to x\}.$$

Prove or disprove: for every two distinct points $p,q\in\Gamma(\{\gamma_k\})$, at least one of the following two alternatives must hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the open real segment $\{tp+(1-t)q : 0<t<1\}$ is contained in $\Omega$; or
\item the closed real segment $\{tp+(1-t)q : 0\le t\le 1\}$ is contained in $\partial\Omega$, and the complex affine line through $p$ and $q$, namely $\mathbb{C}(p-q)+q$, does not intersect $\Omega$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in a 2025 collection of open questions about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in $\mathbb{C}^N$. Related works (e.g., on non-visibility of Kobayashi geodesics and boundary geometry, 2023–2024) describe partial results — such as that limit sets of non-visible geodesics lie in real segments inside complex hyperplane sections of the boundary in certain smooth cases — but no source found resolves the general conjecture, which appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in C^N
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 3.5 states the dichotomy for cluster sets of non-visible geodesic sequences in bounded convex domains in C^N.
status_evidence.claim: The dichotomy is explicitly posed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On non-visibility of Kobayashi geodesics and the geometry of the boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geometry of boundary cluster sets of non-visible Kobayashi geodesics, showing in smooth convex cases that such limit sets lie in real segments contained in complex hyperplane sections of the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results in special (smooth) cases support the conjectural picture but do not establish the general statement.

status_evidence.title: Visibility of Kobayashi geodesics in convex domains and related properties
status_evidence.snippet: Develops visibility property framework for convex domains; provides background but does not prove the general dichotomy of Conjecture 3.5.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational visibility framework, conjecture remains unresolved in general.
